sections.h2: Who sets and collects property tax in Geauga County
sections.html:
Three county offices in Chardon share the work. The Auditor puts a value on every parcel, the Treasurer mails the bills and receives the money, and the Board of Revision rules on disputes over value. The Board is made up of the Auditor, its permanent secretary, the president of the County Commissioners and the Treasurer.

The Auditor's office is at 231 Main Street, Suite 1-A, Chardon, Ohio 44024. The real estate direct line is (440) 279-1617, and the main line is (440) 279-1600.

Two tools on the Auditor's Tax Info page are worth bookmarking: a Calculate Your Taxes page that estimates the bill on an existing or hypothetical parcel, and a Tax Rates page. Rates start with the Geauga County Budget Commission, are certified by each taxing district to the Auditor, and are then adjusted by the state's effective-rate factors each December. Levy changes are listed for each of the 33 districts. Some levies are non-qualifying, meaning the 10 percent and Owner Occupancy credits do not apply to them.

First-half bills go out in January and second-half bills in June. Payment deadlines fall on the second Wednesday in February and the second Wednesday in July. A yearly tax calendar on the Auditor's portal gives the exact dates.

The Treasurer sends tax bills only by regular mail. Any text message asking for a tax payment is fraudulent.

  • The Treasurer, not the Auditor, issues the bills.
  • Any text asking you to pay is a scam, so delete it.
  • Before a closing, request a payoff on the exact parcel from the Treasurer.

On January 1, 2026 the Auditor's portal counted 52,207 parcels in Geauga County. The Auditor's office must see that every parcel and the buildings on it are fairly and uniformly appraised.

Each of the 33 taxing districts carries its own levies, which is why identical houses in different townships or school districts can get different bills.

State law has every parcel reappraised at six-year intervals, with a mid-cycle update in year three. The Auditor's appraisal office handles the sexennial reappraisals, the triennial updates and annual new construction valuations. Its field appraisers visit every property that was issued a building or zoning permit during the year.

Tentative values for tax year 2026, payable in 2027, are posted on the Auditor's portal, where owners can search by parcel. Added square footage, additions, new outbuildings and major improvements that needed a permit change a value. New carpet, appliances, fixtures, landscaping and a new driveway surface do not.

Start by asking one of the Auditor's appraisers for an informal review. If you still disagree, file a formal complaint with the Board of Revision. The appraisal office wants solid evidence for at least one of these three grounds.

  • The record describes the property wrongly, for instance a carport listed as a garage.
  • The estimate runs above what comparable homes sold for, or above a bank appraisal.
  • Your value is out of line with the estimates on similar homes nearby.

R.C. 5715.19 gives owners until the end of March after the tax year, or until first-half collection closes if that falls later. The Board then has 180 days from the final filing date to rule. While a complaint is open the Treasurer will take payment at your claimed value, and interest accrues on any gap if you lose. A parcel already challenged during the same interim period cannot be challenged again unless it sold at arm's length, lost value to casualty or gained a major improvement.

The Homestead Exemption shields $29,000 of a home's market value from local taxes, and the average Geauga savings is about $518 a year. In the Auditor's example, a $100,000 home would be billed as if it were worth $71,000.

  • Seniors: turn 65 by the end of 2026 and keep household income below $41,000, measured as 2025 Ohio adjusted gross income.
  • Disabled owners: certified permanently and totally disabled on January 1, 2026, under the same income cap.
  • Disabled service members: hold a total (100 percent) service-connected rating and file form DTE 105I.
  • Surviving spouses: of someone who was getting the old exemption, if at least 59 when the spouse died.

File a paper application, DTE 105A, with the Auditor by December 31. The signature must be original, and electronic filing is not accepted. If the Auditor denies you, form DTE 106B carries the appeal to the Board of Revision. The Auditor also runs an Owner Occupancy Credit tool, the farm CAUV and forestry programs and a destroyed property deduction.

The Auditor can lower the value of real estate hurt by fire, flood, ice or other causes, but cannot issue refunds for earlier years. File the damaged property application as soon as possible. The deduction depends on the calendar quarter of the damage.

Damage from January through March earns a 100 percent deduction and April through June earns 75 percent, and the deadline for both is December 31. July through September earns 50 percent with the same deadline. October through December earns 25 percent, with a January 31 deadline. The reduction stays until the property is restored.

sections.h2: Taxes at a Geauga County closing
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Auditor for transfer before they are recorded. The Auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of transfer value plus $0.50 per parcel, and the tax records are updated as the parcel changes hands.

Get the balance on the parcel from the Treasurer, then confirm with your title company who pays the February and July installments. If taxes on a parcel were missed, the Auditor's Forfeited Land Sale page is the place to look. A cash sale needs the same payoff figure, so request it before you set a closing date.

The 2020 count was 95,397 people. Owners occupy 87.2 percent of the housing stock, the median home they own is worth $331,100, and the median household earns $107,860. The county issued 180 building permits in 2025. Chardon, Burton, Middlefield and South Russell are among its municipalities, and a November 2024 vote dissolved the Village of Aquilla.

faqs.q: When are Geauga County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The second Wednesday in February covers the first half and the second Wednesday in July covers the second half. The Treasurer mails the bills ahead of each date, in January and June.

faqs.q: How much can the Geauga County homestead exemption save?
faqs.a: The exemption shields $29,000 of market value, with average savings of about $518 a year. You must apply on paper with the Auditor by December 31 and meet the age or disability and income rules.

faqs.q: Where does a Geauga County value dispute start?
faqs.a: Ask the Auditor's appraisal office for an informal review first. If that fails, a complaint to the Board of Revision must reach the Auditor by the end of the following March, or when first-half collection closes if that is later.

faqs.q: Will the Geauga County Treasurer text me a tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer sends bills only by regular mail. A text message asking for a tax payment is fraudulent and should be deleted.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Geauga County real estate tax staff?
faqs.a: Questions about values, exemptions and credits go to the Auditor's real estate line, (440) 279-1617. The main Auditor number is (440) 279-1600, answered on weekdays between 8:00 and 4:30.
